concepts.def: Loss of electrons, or gain of oxygen.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Redox, Rusting & Iron — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Redox, Rusting & Iron brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Redox, Rusting & Iron.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In the blast furnace, iron(III) oxide is reduced mainly by:
options: Carbon monoxide
Oxygen
Limestone
Slag

mcqs.q: Zinc protects iron sacrificially because zinc:
options: Is more reactive and is oxidised in preference to the iron
Is less reactive than iron
Forms an alloy with the rust
Absorbs the water before it reaches the iron
Loss of electrons
Gain of electrons
Gain of hydrogen
Loss of oxygen

mcqs.q: Does iron rust in completely dry air?
options: A scratched zinc coating turns the iron into steel.
Iron rusts whenever it is exposed to air, even if the air is perfectly dry.
Iron only rusts when it is touching an acid.
No — rusting needs both oxygen and water; removing either one stops it, which is the basis of rust prevention.

mcqs.q: If a zinc coating is scratched, does the iron underneath rust quickly?
options: Once galvanising is scratched, the iron rusts just as fast as bare iron.
A scratched zinc coating turns the iron into steel.
Iron only rusts when it is touching an acid.
No — zinc is more reactive than iron, so it is oxidised in preference and still protects the exposed iron sacrificially.
Rusting is the iron slowly melting in the rain.
Rusting is just the iron getting wet and stained, not a real chemical change.
A scratched zinc coating turns the iron into steel.
Yes — it is a redox reaction in which iron is oxidised, forming a new substance, hydrated iron(III) oxide.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Reduction”?
options: A reaction in which oxidation and reduction happen together: one species is oxidised while another is reduced.
The corrosion of iron to hydrated iron(III) oxide; it requires both oxygen and water to be present.
The loss of oxygen or the gain of electrons by a substance; its oxidation state decreases.
Iron is extracted from its ore haematite, Fe₂O₃, by reduction with carbon monoxide in a blast furnace.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Rusting”?
options: Barriers such as paint, oil or grease keep out air and water; galvanising with zinc also gives sacrificial protection.
The corrosion of iron to hydrated iron(III) oxide; it requires both oxygen and water to be present.
A reaction in which oxidation and reduction happen together: one species is oxidised while another is reduced.
The loss of oxygen or the gain of electrons by a substance; its oxidation state decreases.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Rust prevention”?
options: The corrosion of iron to hydrated iron(III) oxide; it requires both oxygen and water to be present.
A reaction in which oxidation and reduction happen together: one species is oxidised while another is reduced.
The loss of oxygen or the gain of electrons by a substance; its oxidation state decreases.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Redox reaction”?
options: The loss of oxygen or the gain of electrons by a substance; its oxidation state decreases.
Barriers such as paint, oil or grease keep out air and water; galvanising with zinc also gives sacrificial protection.

sequence.def: Oxygen AND water both reach the metal surface
Iron atoms lose electrons, forming Fe2+ ions
Fe2+ becomes Fe3+ as oxygen keeps attacking
Orange-brown rust builds up on the surface
Rust is porous, so corrosion eats ever deeper
